articles.title: DWP cyber incident ‘probably an attack’, says former UK chief technology officer
articles.snippet: Government took down pensions and benefits portal on Thursday but said regular payments will not be affected A serious cyber incident that forced ministers to take down online benefits and pension services was “probably an attack”, the UK’s former chief technology officer has said. The Department for Work and Pensions took down several systems that appeared to still be offline on Saturday morning. David Knott, who led government technology until December 2025, said much infrastructure was outdated, and underinvestment in defence and increasing sophistication of attacks meant it was only getting more vulnerable. Chris O’Shea, the chief executive of Centrica, reportedly told staff at the Rough gas storage facility off the east Yorkshire that the government had rebuffed the company’s plea for short-term support to run the store over the winter. articles.title: Norse Atlantic Airways files for bankruptcy and cancels all future flights
articles.snippet: Norwegian airline tells customers not to come to airports after surging fuel costs caused by Iran war ruin finances Norse Atlantic Airways has filed for bankruptcy and cancelled all future flights after surging fuel costs caused by the Iran war ruined its finances. The Norwegian airline said it was entering insolvency and posted a message on its website telling customers not to come to airports – including passengers stranded away from home. Its collapse came a day after it put flights on hold with a warning that its finances were critical. Continue reading...
